name: Codex
description: OpenAI's Codex CLI, headless: one codex exec process per turn, resumed into a single thread. It can ask the user questions through the colonizer MCP server; the runner fetches the pinned codex binary into its cache on first boot, so nothing needs to be staged into the colony image.

requires.image: glibc + node >= 20; the runner fetches the pinned @openai/codex CLI itself

session_resume.description: Codex keeps every session rollout under CODEX_HOME and can resume any thread given its id, so a colony waiting on the user can be suspended (its microVM stopped) and continued with the conversation intact; the runner strips the mounted dir back to the rollout store on every boot.

model.title: Orchestrator model
model.description: Model for the colony as openai/<model> or a bare OpenAI model id, passed to codex exec -m. Empty (the default) passes no -m: Codex runs on the CLI's own default model. A <provider>/<model> whose prefix matches a connection from Settings → Model providers rides the mothership's gateway on its openai wire instead — tokens and spend are accounted host-side and no OpenAI key is needed in the colony. Anthropic-wire connections and providers with no route are refused: codex speaks the OpenAI wire only.

subagent_model.title: Subagent model
subagent_model.description: Accepted for parity with the other agent modules, but unused: headless codex exec has no subagent split, every turn runs on the orchestrator model.

background_model.title: Background model
background_model.description: Accepted for parity with the other agent modules, but unused: headless codex exec has no background-worker split, every turn runs on the orchestrator model.

disabled_tools.title: Disabled tools
disabled_tools.description: Comma-separated Codex tool names this colony never gets: shell (the shell tool), web_search or view_image. Each rides every turn as a -c config override, behind --strict-config so a key codex stops recognising fails the turn instead of silently keeping the tool. apply_patch (Codex's own file-editing tool) and MCP tools cannot be turned off. Empty disables nothing.
